description: This module covers AWS AI/ML services and their real-world applications across industries. It focuses on understanding which AWS service to select for specific use cases, including computer vision, natural language processing, speech processing, document analysis, intelligent search, personalization, forecasting, fraud detection, and AI-powered developer tools. Mastery of this module requires the ability to match business scenarios to the correct AWS AI service and understand how these services integrate into industry-specific solutions for healthcare, finance, retail, and manufacturing.

topics.definition: Amazon Rekognition is a fully managed computer vision service that uses deep learning to analyze images and videos. It can identify objects, people, text, scenes, and activities, as well as detect inappropriate content. Key features include facial analysis and recognition, celebrity recognition, custom label detection for domain-specific objects, Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) detection, and video segment detection. Rekognition provides confidence scores for its detections and supports both real-time streaming video analysis and batch image processing. It requires no machine learning expertise and is commonly used in media, public safety, and identity verification scenarios.

Amazon Comprehend is a fully managed Natural Language Processing (NLP) service that uses machine learning to extract insights and relationships from unstructured text. It performs sentiment analysis (positive, negative, neutral, mixed), entity recognition (people, places, organizations, dates), key phrase extraction, language detection (over 100 languages), syntax analysis, and topic modeling. Amazon Comprehend Medical is a specialized variant that extracts medical information such as conditions, medications, dosages, and procedures from clinical text. Comprehend also supports custom entity recognition and custom classification, enabling organizations to train models tailored to their specific domain terminology.

Amazon Transcribe is an automatic speech recognition (ASR) service that converts speech to text. It supports real-time streaming transcription and batch processing of audio files. Key features include custom vocabularies for domain-specific terminology, automatic content redaction for personally identifiable information (PII), speaker diarization to identify individual speakers, channel identification for multi-channel audio, and automatic language identification. Amazon Transcribe Medical is a specialized variant optimized for medical conversations that is HIPAA-eligible. Amazon Transcribe Call Analytics provides turn-by-turn call transcription with built-in analytics such as call categorization, sentiment detection, and issue detection.

Amazon Polly is a text-to-speech (TTS) service that uses advanced deep learning technologies to synthesize natural-sounding human speech from text. It supports dozens of languages and offers a variety of lifelike voices including standard and Neural Text-to-Speech (NTTS) voices. Polly supports Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) for fine-grained control over pronunciation, volume, pitch, and speaking rate. It also supports lexicons for customizing pronunciation of specific words and the Newscaster speaking style for news narration use cases. Polly is commonly used for accessibility features, interactive voice response (IVR) systems, e-learning content, and content creation.

Amazon Translate is a neural machine translation service that delivers fast, high-quality, affordable, and customizable language translation. It supports translation across 75+ languages and enables real-time and batch translation workflows. Key features include Active Custom Translation for domain-specific translations using parallel data, automatic source language detection, formality customization, profanity masking, and brevity settings. Translate integrates with other AWS services and is commonly used for localizing websites and applications, translating user-generated content, enabling multilingual communication, and processing large volumes of documents in multiple languages.

Amazon Lex is a fully managed AI service for building conversational interfaces (chatbots and voice bots) into applications using voice and text. It uses the same conversational engine and deep learning technologies that power Amazon Alexa. Key concepts include intents (actions the user wants to perform), utterances (phrases that trigger intents), slots (data the bot needs to collect), and fulfillment (the business logic executed after slot values are collected). Lex supports multi-turn conversations, context management, session attributes, and integration with AWS Lambda for fulfillment logic. It connects natively to Amazon Connect for contact center deployments and supports deployment across messaging platforms and web applications.

Amazon Textract is a machine learning service that automatically extracts text, handwriting, and structured data from scanned documents. Unlike simple OCR, Textract understands the layout and relationships within documents, extracting data from tables, forms (key-value pairs), and complex structured documents. It supports Queries, which allow natural language questions to be asked about a document, and specialized APIs for analyzing expense documents (invoices and receipts), identity documents (passports and driver licenses), and lending documents. Textract outputs structured JSON with confidence scores and bounding box coordinates, making it suitable for automating document processing workflows in finance, healthcare, legal, and government sectors.

Amazon Kendra is an intelligent enterprise search service powered by machine learning. Unlike keyword-based search engines, Kendra uses natural language understanding to return precise answers to natural language questions from across an organization's data sources. It supports over 40 built-in connectors for popular data sources including Amazon S3, SharePoint, Salesforce, ServiceNow, databases, and websites. Kendra provides document ranking based on relevance, access control that respects existing permissions, and incremental learning from user feedback. It supports custom document enrichment and FAQs, and its response types include factoid answers (specific facts), descriptive answers (passages), and document results (ranked list of relevant documents).

Amazon Personalize is a fully managed machine learning service that makes it easy to create individualized recommendations for customers. It uses the same recommendation technology used by Amazon.com. Personalize supports multiple recipe types including user personalization (personalized recommendations per user), related items (similar item recommendations), and personalized ranking (re-ranking a list of items for a specific user). It ingests three types of data: user interactions (behavioral data like clicks and purchases), item metadata (catalog information), and user metadata (demographic information). Personalize supports real-time event ingestion, contextual recommendations based on device type or time of day, and business rule filters to apply constraints to recommendations.

topics.topicName: Amazon Forecast, Amazon Fraud Detector, and Amazon Q Developer
topics.definition: Amazon Forecast is a fully managed time-series forecasting service that uses machine learning to generate accurate forecasts from historical time-series data. It automatically examines data, selects algorithms, trains models, and provides forecasts up to 50% more accurate than traditional methods, with applications in demand planning, financial planning, and resource planning. Amazon Fraud Detector is a fully managed service that uses machine learning and Amazon's fraud detection expertise to identify potentially fraudulent online activities such as fake account creation, online payment fraud, and loyalty program abuse. It allows creation of custom fraud detection models using your data without requiring ML expertise. Amazon Q Developer (formerly Amazon CodeWhisperer) is a generative AI-powered coding assistant that provides real-time code suggestions, security vulnerability scanning, code transformation, and natural language chat for software development tasks. It supports multiple programming languages and IDEs, and helps developers write code faster while following security best practices.

questions.question: A media company wants to automatically detect and blur faces in video content before broadcasting. Which AWS service is BEST suited for this task?
questions.explanation: Amazon Rekognition is the correct choice because it provides facial detection and analysis capabilities for both images and videos. It can identify faces in video content with bounding box coordinates, which can then be used to apply blurring. Comprehend is for NLP text analysis, Textract is for document processing, and Translate is for language translation — none of which handle video face detection.

questions.question: A healthcare organization needs to extract medication names, dosages, and medical conditions from unstructured clinical notes. Which AWS service should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend Medical is specifically designed to extract medical information from unstructured clinical text, including medication names, dosages, conditions, treatments, and procedures. While Amazon Textract can extract text from documents, it does not understand medical terminology or relationships. Amazon Kendra is a search service, and Rekognition handles image/video analysis.

questions.question: A company wants to build an interactive chatbot for its customer service website that can understand natural language and route requests to the correct department. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate?
questions.explanation: Amazon Lex is the correct service for building conversational chatbots and voice bots. It uses NLU (Natural Language Understanding) to interpret user intents and can be configured with intents, utterances, and slots to route requests to the appropriate department. Polly converts text to speech, Kendra is for intelligent search, and Transcribe converts speech to text.

questions.question: An e-commerce company wants to show personalized product recommendations to each customer on its homepage. Which AWS service should they choose?
questions.explanation: Amazon Personalize is designed specifically for generating individualized recommendations for users. It uses the same recommendation technology as Amazon.com and can provide personalized product suggestions based on user interaction data, item metadata, and user metadata. Forecast is for time-series predictions, Comprehend is for text analysis, and Kendra is for enterprise search.

questions.question: A multinational corporation needs to translate its product documentation from English into 15 different languages in bulk. Which AWS service is MOST suitable?
questions.explanation: Amazon Translate is a neural machine translation service that supports 75+ languages and can perform both real-time and batch translations. It is ideal for translating large volumes of product documentation across multiple languages. Comprehend analyzes text but does not translate it, Polly converts text to speech, and Transcribe converts speech to text.

questions.question: A company processes thousands of invoices daily and needs to automatically extract vendor names, dates, line items, and totals. Which AWS service provides the BEST solution?
questions.explanation: Amazon Textract is specifically designed to extract text, forms, tables, and structured data from documents. Its AnalyzeExpense API is purpose-built for processing invoices and receipts, extracting fields like vendor names, dates, line items, and totals with high accuracy. Comprehend analyzes text for sentiment and entities but does not process document layouts, Rekognition handles images/video for object detection, and Kendra is for search.

questions.question: A retail company wants to predict demand for its products over the next 3 months to optimize inventory levels. Which AWS service should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Forecast is a managed time-series forecasting service ideal for demand forecasting. It uses machine learning to analyze historical sales data and generate accurate predictions for future demand, which helps companies optimize inventory levels. Personalize is for recommendations, Fraud Detector is for detecting fraudulent activities, and Comprehend is for NLP text analysis.

questions.question: A call center wants to transcribe customer calls in real-time and identify the sentiment of each speaker during the conversation. Which combination of AWS services is MOST appropriate?
questions.explanation: Amazon Transcribe Call Analytics is purpose-built for this use case. It provides turn-by-turn call transcription along with built-in analytics including sentiment detection, call categorization, and issue detection for each speaker. It combines transcription and analytics in a single service, eliminating the need to chain multiple services together.

questions.question: A construction company wants to ensure workers are wearing the required safety equipment (hard hats, vests, gloves) on job sites by analyzing security camera feeds. Which AWS service should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Rekognition has a specific feature for Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) detection that can identify whether people in images or video are wearing the required safety equipment such as hard hats, face covers, and hand covers. This makes it ideal for monitoring workplace safety compliance through security camera analysis.

questions.question: A financial institution wants to automatically detect fraudulent new account registrations on its online banking platform. Which AWS service is specifically designed for this purpose?
questions.explanation: Amazon Fraud Detector is specifically designed to identify potentially fraudulent online activities, including fake account creation, online payment fraud, and loyalty program abuse. It uses machine learning and Amazon's fraud detection expertise to build custom fraud detection models. Forecast is for time-series predictions, Comprehend is for text analysis, and Personalize is for recommendations.

questions.question: A news organization wants to convert its text articles into audio format so visually impaired users can listen to the news. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate?
questions.explanation: Amazon Polly is a text-to-speech service that converts text into natural-sounding speech. It supports the Newscaster speaking style specifically designed for news narration use cases, making it ideal for converting news articles into audio format for accessibility. Transcribe converts speech to text (the opposite), Translate handles language translation, and Lex is for chatbots.

questions.question: An enterprise wants to enable employees to search internal knowledge bases, wikis, and documentation using natural language questions and receive precise answers. Which AWS service should they implement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Kendra is an intelligent enterprise search service that uses natural language understanding to provide precise answers from across organizational data sources. It supports over 40 built-in connectors for popular data sources and returns factoid answers, descriptive passages, and ranked document results. Comprehend analyzes text but does not provide search, Textract processes documents, and Lex builds chatbots.

questions.question: A developer wants an AI-powered tool that provides real-time code suggestions and identifies security vulnerabilities while coding in their IDE. Which AWS offering provides this capability?
questions.explanation: Amazon Q Developer (formerly Amazon CodeWhisperer) is a generative AI-powered coding assistant that provides real-time code suggestions, security vulnerability scanning, and natural language chat directly within IDEs. It supports multiple programming languages and helps developers write code faster while following security best practices. The other services are not designed for code development assistance.

questions.question: A social media platform wants to automatically detect and filter inappropriate content from user-uploaded images. Which AWS service provides this capability?
questions.explanation: Amazon Rekognition provides content moderation capabilities that can detect inappropriate, unwanted, or offensive content in images and videos. It can identify various categories of unsafe content and return confidence scores, enabling platforms to automatically filter or flag user-uploaded images. Comprehend works with text, Textract processes documents, and Kendra is for search.

questions.question: A company wants to analyze thousands of customer reviews to determine overall sentiment (positive, negative, neutral) about their products. Which AWS service is BEST suited for this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend provides sentiment analysis as a core NLP capability. It can analyze text and classify sentiment as positive, negative, neutral, or mixed, making it ideal for analyzing customer reviews at scale. Personalize is for recommendations, Kendra is for search, and Forecast is for time-series predictions.

questions.question: A hospital wants to transcribe doctor-patient conversations while ensuring compliance with healthcare privacy regulations. Which AWS service should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Transcribe Medical is a HIPAA-eligible speech recognition service specifically optimized for transcribing medical conversations. It is trained on medical terminology and is designed for healthcare use cases where regulatory compliance (such as HIPAA) is required. Standard Amazon Transcribe is not optimized for medical terminology, Polly is text-to-speech, and Comprehend Medical analyzes text but does not transcribe audio.

questions.question: A streaming service wants to add 'Because you watched X' recommendation rows to its homepage. The company has historical user viewing data. Which AWS service should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Personalize provides a 'related items' recipe type that can generate recommendations similar to items a user has interacted with, exactly like 'Because you watched X' suggestions. It uses historical interaction data to build personalized recommendation models. Kendra is for search, Forecast is for time-series predictions, and Comprehend is for text analysis.

questions.question: A government agency wants to process passport applications by automatically extracting information from passport photos and identity documents. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate?
questions.explanation: Amazon Textract has a specialized AnalyzeID API designed specifically for extracting information from identity documents such as passports and driver licenses. It can extract fields like name, date of birth, document number, and expiration date. While Rekognition can detect faces, it does not extract structured text from identity documents. Comprehend is for text analysis, and Translate is for language translation.

questions.question: Which Amazon Comprehend capability allows organizations to train a model that recognizes entity types specific to their business domain?
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend's custom entity recognition allows organizations to train custom models that can identify entity types specific to their domain. For example, a manufacturing company could train a model to recognize specific part numbers, product codes, or machine names that standard entity recognition would not identify. Sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and language detection are built-in capabilities that do not allow custom entity type training.

questions.question: A contact center uses Amazon Connect and wants to add a virtual agent that handles common customer inquiries before routing to a live agent. Which AWS service integrates natively with Amazon Connect for this purpose?
questions.explanation: Amazon Lex integrates natively with Amazon Connect to provide virtual agent (chatbot and voice bot) capabilities in contact centers. Lex handles natural language understanding, collects required information through multi-turn conversations, and can route to human agents when needed. While Kendra and Polly can also integrate with Connect, Lex is the primary service for building the conversational virtual agent.

questions.question: A company wants to automatically redact personally identifiable information (PII) from audio recordings of customer calls. Which AWS service supports this feature?
questions.explanation: Amazon Transcribe supports automatic content redaction, which can identify and redact PII from transcribed audio. This feature can mask sensitive information such as names, addresses, credit card numbers, and Social Security numbers in the output transcript. Polly generates speech, Comprehend detects PII in text but does not process audio, and Rekognition handles images/video.

questions.question: A retail company has historical sales data for the past 5 years and wants to predict sales for the upcoming holiday season at each store location. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate?
questions.explanation: Amazon Forecast is a time-series forecasting service that uses machine learning to analyze historical data and generate forecasts. It can incorporate related time-series data (like promotions and weather) and metadata (like store location) to produce accurate, granular sales forecasts. Personalize is for recommendations, Comprehend is for text analysis, and Fraud Detector is for detecting fraudulent activities.

questions.question: In Amazon Lex, what are the phrases a user might say to trigger a specific action called?
questions.explanation: In Amazon Lex, utterances are the phrases or sentences that a user might say to invoke a specific intent. For example, 'I want to book a flight' and 'Book me a flight' are different utterances that could trigger the same BookFlight intent. Slots are the data values the bot needs to collect, intents represent the actions the user wants to perform, and fulfillment is the business logic executed after all required data is collected.

questions.question: A logistics company wants to identify text on shipping labels from photos taken by warehouse workers. Which AWS service should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Rekognition's text detection feature can identify and extract text that appears in images, including text on signs, labels, and packaging. For photos of shipping labels taken in a warehouse environment, Rekognition's DetectText API is the most appropriate choice. While Textract excels at extracting text from scanned documents, Rekognition is better suited for text in natural/real-world images. Comprehend works with existing text, and Translate handles language translation.

questions.question: A legal firm needs to process thousands of contracts and extract key terms, clauses, and parties involved from each document. They need to understand the table and form structure within these documents. Which AWS service is BEST suited?
questions.explanation: Amazon Textract is best suited because it extracts text, forms (key-value pairs), and tables from documents while understanding document layout and structure. It can process contracts at scale and extract structured data from complex document formats. Comprehend can analyze the extracted text but cannot process document layouts. Kendra searches documents but does not extract structured data from them. Rekognition is for image/video analysis.

questions.question: Which type of data does Amazon Personalize NOT require as input?
questions.explanation: Amazon Personalize ingests three types of data: user interactions (such as clicks, views, and purchases), item metadata (catalog information like category and price), and user metadata (demographic information like age and location). Audio recordings are not a valid input data type for Personalize. Audio data would be processed by services like Amazon Transcribe.

questions.question: A news website supports readers in 30 countries and wants to automatically translate user comments into the reader's preferred language. The translations must be near real-time. Which AWS service should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Translate supports real-time translation across 75+ languages, making it ideal for translating user-generated content like comments on the fly. It provides low-latency neural machine translation that can handle the near real-time requirement. Comprehend analyzes text but does not translate, Polly converts text to speech, and Transcribe converts speech to text.

questions.question: A manufacturing company wants to detect defects on products moving along a conveyor belt using camera footage. They need to train a model using their own product images since the defects are specific to their domain. Which Amazon Rekognition feature should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels allows customers to train custom computer vision models for domain-specific use cases by providing their own labeled images. This is ideal for manufacturing quality inspection where defect types are specific to the company's products and are not covered by Rekognition's built-in detection capabilities. Celebrity recognition, content moderation, and facial analysis are pre-built features not suitable for custom manufacturing defect detection.

questions.question: A financial services company needs to analyze earnings call transcripts to detect the overall tone and sentiment of each speaker. Which combination of AWS services would be MOST effective?
questions.explanation: Amazon Transcribe would first convert the earnings call audio into text, and then Amazon Comprehend would perform sentiment analysis on the transcribed text to determine the tone and sentiment of each speaker. Transcribe supports speaker diarization to identify different speakers. Polly and Translate do not analyze sentiment, Lex and Kendra are for chatbots and search respectively, and Textract and Rekognition are for documents and images.

questions.question: Which Amazon Polly feature allows fine-grained control over pronunciation, emphasis, pauses, and speaking rate in generated speech?
questions.explanation: SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) is a W3C standard supported by Amazon Polly that provides fine-grained control over speech synthesis including pronunciation, emphasis, pauses, volume, pitch, and speaking rate. Custom vocabularies are a Transcribe feature, speaker diarization is also a Transcribe feature. While Polly lexicons can customize pronunciation of specific words, they do not provide the comprehensive control that SSML offers.

questions.question: A bank wants to detect if credit card transactions are fraudulent in real time. They have historical transaction data labeled as fraudulent or legitimate. Which AWS service is MOST appropriate?
questions.explanation: Amazon Fraud Detector is specifically designed to detect potentially fraudulent online activities including payment fraud. It can use historical labeled data (fraudulent vs. legitimate transactions) to train custom fraud detection models. Forecast is for time-series predictions, Personalize is for recommendations, and Comprehend is for text analysis.

questions.question: A company's IT help desk receives thousands of support tickets daily. They want to automatically categorize each ticket into predefined categories (hardware, software, network, access). Which AWS service and feature should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend's custom classification feature allows organizations to train a custom text classifier using their own labeled data to categorize text into predefined categories. This is ideal for automatically routing support tickets into categories like hardware, software, network, or access. Kendra FAQs provide answers to common questions, Lex intents are for chatbot conversations, and Textract processes document layouts.

questions.question: A video streaming platform wants to automatically tag celebrity appearances in its content library to improve searchability. Which Amazon Rekognition feature should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Rekognition's celebrity recognition feature can automatically identify well-known individuals in images and video content. This is specifically designed for tagging celebrity appearances in media content. Custom Labels is for training domain-specific models, content moderation is for detecting inappropriate content, and text detection identifies text in images.

questions.question: An energy company wants to predict electricity demand for the next 7 days to optimize power generation scheduling. They have 10 years of historical consumption data along with weather data. Which AWS service should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Forecast is designed for time-series forecasting and can incorporate related time-series data (like weather data) alongside the primary time-series (electricity consumption) to generate more accurate forecasts. It automatically selects the best algorithm and handles the complexities of time-series analysis. While SageMaker could be used, Forecast provides a managed, no-code experience specifically for this use case.

questions.question: Which Amazon Kendra response type returns a specific, concise answer extracted from a document, such as a date or name?
questions.explanation: Amazon Kendra's factoid answer type returns specific, concise answers to questions that expect a fact, such as 'When was the company founded?' returning '1999.' Descriptive answers return longer passages that explain a concept, document responses return a ranked list of relevant documents, and 'suggested answer' is not a Kendra response type.

questions.question: A company wants to enable their existing Amazon Lex chatbot to make outbound phone calls to customers. Which AWS service should they integrate with?
questions.explanation: Amazon Connect is a cloud-based contact center service that natively integrates with Amazon Lex. It can handle both inbound and outbound phone calls, and when integrated with Lex, it enables the chatbot to conduct voice-based conversations over the phone. While Polly provides text-to-speech capability that Lex uses internally, Connect provides the telephony infrastructure. Transcribe is for speech-to-text, and Pinpoint is for marketing communications.

questions.question: A media company receives audio content in multiple languages and wants to automatically detect which language is being spoken before transcribing it. Which Amazon Transcribe feature supports this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Transcribe's automatic language identification feature can detect the dominant language in an audio file before or during transcription, eliminating the need to manually specify the language. Custom vocabularies add domain-specific terms, speaker diarization identifies individual speakers, and channel identification separates audio from different channels.

questions.question: A pharmaceutical company wants to search across millions of research papers, clinical trial reports, and internal documentation to find answers to scientific questions. Which AWS service should they implement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Kendra is an intelligent search service that uses natural language understanding to search across large document repositories and return precise answers. It supports over 40 data source connectors and can ingest documents from various sources. Comprehend analyzes text for insights but does not provide search functionality, Textract extracts data from individual documents, and Translate handles language translation.

questions.question: A ride-sharing company wants to verify driver identities by comparing a selfie taken during login with the photo on their registered driver license. Which AWS service should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Rekognition provides face comparison (CompareFaces API) that can compare a face in one image against a face in another image to determine if they are the same person. This is ideal for identity verification by comparing a live selfie to a reference photo from an identity document. Textract extracts text from documents, Comprehend analyzes text, and Kendra is for search.

questions.question: Which data type is REQUIRED (not optional) for Amazon Personalize to generate recommendations?
questions.explanation: User interactions (behavioral data such as clicks, views, and purchases) is the only required data type for Amazon Personalize. Item metadata and user metadata are optional but can improve recommendation quality. Contextual metadata (like device type or time of day) is also optional and used for contextual recommendations.

questions.question: A company wants to build a voice-enabled IVR (Interactive Voice Response) system that greets callers and routes them based on spoken requests. Which combination of AWS services forms the foundation of this solution?

options.A: Amazon Transcribe, Amazon Comprehend, Amazon Polly

questions.explanation: Amazon Lex provides the conversational AI capabilities (speech recognition and natural language understanding) while Amazon Connect provides the cloud telephony infrastructure for the IVR system. Together they handle voice input, intent recognition, and call routing. Lex already includes speech-to-text and text-to-speech capabilities internally, so separate Transcribe, Comprehend, and Polly services are not needed for basic IVR functionality.

questions.question: A company uses Amazon Translate for its customer support platform but finds that industry-specific terms are not being translated correctly. How can they improve translation quality for these terms?

options.B: Use Active Custom Translation with parallel data

questions.explanation: Amazon Translate's Active Custom Translation feature allows users to provide parallel data (pairs of source and target sentences) that customize translation output for domain-specific terminology. This improves translation quality for industry-specific terms. Comprehend is for text analysis not translation, Transcribe is for speech-to-text, and Polly lexicons customize pronunciation in speech synthesis.

questions.question: A healthcare company wants to extract patient information from handwritten intake forms. Which AWS service can handle handwritten text extraction?
questions.explanation: Amazon Textract can extract both printed and handwritten text from documents, along with form data (key-value pairs) and tables. This makes it ideal for processing handwritten intake forms where patients fill in information by hand. Comprehend analyzes existing digital text, Rekognition focuses on image/video analysis (objects, faces, etc.), and Kendra is for enterprise search.

questions.question: An airline wants to re-rank its search results page for each individual customer so that the most relevant flights appear first based on that customer's travel history and preferences. Which Amazon Personalize recipe type should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Personalize's personalized ranking recipe re-ranks a provided list of items for a specific user based on their predicted interest. This is ideal for re-ranking search results (like flight options) to show the most relevant results first for each customer. User personalization generates a list of recommended items, related items finds similar items, and popularity count is not a Personalize recipe type.

questions.question: A company processes conference call recordings that have multiple participants speaking on separate audio channels. Which Amazon Transcribe feature should they enable to get separate transcripts for each participant?
questions.explanation: Channel identification in Amazon Transcribe is used when each participant is on a separate audio channel (common in conference call systems). It produces separate transcripts for each channel. Speaker diarization is used when all speakers share a single audio channel and you need to distinguish between them. Automatic language detection identifies the spoken language, and custom vocabularies add domain-specific terms.

questions.question: A gaming company wants to detect toxic language in player chat messages in real time. Which AWS service should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend provides sentiment analysis and can be used to detect negative sentiment and potentially toxic language in real-time text streams. Its real-time endpoint can classify chat messages as they arrive. For more specific toxicity detection, Comprehend's custom classification could be trained on labeled examples of toxic vs. non-toxic messages. Rekognition handles images/video, Translate handles language translation, and Kendra is for search.

questions.question: A mortgage company wants to automate the processing of lending applications by extracting data from pay stubs, bank statements, and tax forms. Which Amazon Textract feature is specifically designed for this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Textract provides specialized lending document analysis that can automatically classify and extract information from lending-related documents such as pay stubs, bank statements, and tax forms (like W-2s and 1099s). AnalyzeExpense is for invoices and receipts, AnalyzeID is for identity documents, and DetectDocumentText only extracts raw text without understanding document structure.

questions.question: A company wants to detect the language of incoming customer emails before routing them to the appropriate language-specific support team. Which AWS service provides this capability with the LEAST effort?
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend provides a language detection feature that can identify the dominant language in text from over 100 supported languages with a single API call. This is the simplest approach for detecting the language of text-based emails. While Amazon Translate can also detect source language, Comprehend is the more appropriate service when the goal is language identification of text rather than translation.

questions.question: A retail company wants to send personalized marketing emails featuring product recommendations for each subscriber. They have user browsing and purchase history. Which AWS service should power the recommendation engine?
questions.explanation: Amazon Personalize is the correct service for generating personalized product recommendations for individual users. Using the user personalization recipe with browsing and purchase history as interaction data, Personalize can generate unique product recommendations for each email subscriber. Kendra is for search, Forecast is for time-series predictions, and Comprehend is for text analysis.

questions.question: Which statement about Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels is TRUE?

options.A: It requires a minimum of 10,000 labeled images to train a model
options.B: It can only detect objects that are already in Rekognition's built-in model
options.C: It allows users to train custom models to detect domain-specific objects and scenes using their own labeled images
options.D: It requires deep learning expertise to configure and train

questions.explanation: Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels allows users to train custom computer vision models to identify objects and scenes specific to their business needs using their own labeled images. It does not require 10,000 images (it can work with a small number), it is specifically designed to go beyond built-in capabilities, and it requires no deep learning expertise as it automates the model training process.

questions.question: A company has a podcast and wants to generate captions for hearing-impaired listeners. Which AWS service should they use to convert the podcast audio into text?
questions.explanation: Amazon Transcribe is the speech-to-text service that converts audio into accurate text transcriptions, which can be used as captions. It supports features like timestamps that are essential for captioning. Polly converts text to speech (the opposite direction), Comprehend analyzes existing text, and Translate handles language translation.

questions.question: A company wants to ask natural language questions about information in their scanned PDF documents without building a search index. Which Amazon Textract feature supports this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Textract Queries allows users to ask natural language questions about a document, and Textract will return the specific answer extracted from the document. For example, asking 'What is the patient name?' on a medical form. This eliminates the need to build a search index or post-process extracted data. AnalyzeExpense is for invoices, DetectDocumentText extracts raw text, and AnalyzeID is for identity documents.

questions.question: A large enterprise wants its Amazon Kendra search to respect existing document-level access controls so employees only see search results they are authorized to view. Which Kendra feature enables this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Kendra supports access control lists (ACLs) that can filter search results based on user and group permissions. When connected to data sources like SharePoint or Confluence, Kendra can inherit existing access controls to ensure users only see documents they are authorized to view. Document enrichment modifies document metadata, custom ranking adjusts result relevance, and FAQ management handles frequently asked questions.

questions.question: A mobile app developer wants to add real-time language translation to a chat feature so users speaking different languages can communicate seamlessly. Which AWS service should they integrate?
questions.explanation: Amazon Translate provides real-time neural machine translation with low latency, making it suitable for chat applications where messages need to be translated instantly between languages. It supports auto-detection of the source language and translation to the desired target language. Comprehend analyzes text, Lex builds chatbots, and Polly generates speech.

questions.question: An insurance company wants to automatically process claim forms, extracting claimant details from filled-in forms that contain both typed and handwritten information. The forms have a structured layout with labeled fields. Which AWS service feature is MOST relevant?

options.A: Amazon Textract AnalyzeDocument with Forms feature type

questions.explanation: Amazon Textract's AnalyzeDocument API with the Forms feature type extracts key-value pairs from structured forms, handling both typed and handwritten text. It understands form layouts and maps field labels to their values, making it ideal for processing structured claim forms. Comprehend entity recognition works on unstructured text, Rekognition text detection is for text in natural images, and Kendra searches but does not extract form data.

questions.question: A customer wants to use Amazon Personalize but is concerned about showing inappropriate items in recommendations. How can they address this?

options.A: Use Amazon Comprehend to filter results
options.B: Apply filters in Amazon Personalize to exclude specific items based on business rules

questions.explanation: Amazon Personalize supports filters that allow you to apply business rules to recommendations. You can use filter expressions to include or exclude items based on item metadata conditions (e.g., exclude out-of-stock items, items not appropriate for the user's age group, or items in certain categories). This is a built-in feature of Personalize that does not require additional services.

questions.question: A government organization wants to automatically extract entities such as organization names, locations, dates, and quantities from policy documents. Which AWS service provides this capability out of the box?
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend provides built-in entity recognition that can extract entities such as organizations, locations, dates, quantities, and more from text. This is a core NLP capability of Comprehend that works out of the box without training. Textract extracts text from documents but does not classify entities, Kendra provides search, and Translate handles language translation.

questions.question: A music streaming service wants to generate 'Discover Weekly' playlists personalized for each user based on their listening history. Which Amazon Personalize recipe is MOST suitable?
questions.explanation: The user personalization recipe in Amazon Personalize generates a unique list of recommended items for each user based on their interaction history and, optionally, item and user metadata. This is ideal for generating personalized playlists or 'Discover Weekly' type features. Personalized ranking re-ranks an existing list, related items finds similar items to a given item, and 'Trending now' is not a standard Personalize recipe.

questions.question: A company is building an application that needs to convert text to speech in multiple languages and wants the most natural-sounding voices available. Which Amazon Polly voice type should they choose?
questions.explanation: Amazon Polly's Neural Text-to-Speech (NTTS) voices produce the most natural and human-like speech quality. NTTS uses a neural network-based synthesis engine that generates more lifelike speech compared to standard voices. While standard voices are available in more languages, NTTS voices provide superior speech quality. Whisper and conversational are not standard Polly voice categories.

questions.question: A company has deployed a chatbot using Amazon Lex. They want the chatbot to execute backend business logic (such as looking up order status in a database) after collecting all required information from the user. Which Lex concept handles this?
questions.explanation: Fulfillment in Amazon Lex is the mechanism that executes business logic after all required slot values have been collected from the user. Fulfillment typically invokes an AWS Lambda function that performs the backend operation (like querying a database for order status). Utterances trigger intents, slots collect data values, and session attributes store conversation state across turns.

questions.question: An online marketplace wants to detect fraudulent seller accounts that are created to sell counterfeit products. Which AWS service should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Fraud Detector is designed to detect potentially fraudulent online activities, including fake account creation. It can analyze patterns in account registration data to identify potentially fraudulent seller accounts. Personalize is for recommendations, Comprehend is for text analysis, and Forecast is for time-series predictions.

questions.question: A hospital wants to enable doctors to dictate clinical notes using voice, with the transcription understanding medical terms like drug names, procedures, and anatomical references. Which service should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Transcribe Medical is specifically designed for medical speech-to-text transcription. It is pre-trained on medical terminology and understands drug names, procedures, anatomical references, and other medical terms without requiring custom vocabulary setup. It is also HIPAA-eligible. While standard Transcribe with custom vocabulary could work, Transcribe Medical is purpose-built and more accurate for medical use cases. Comprehend Medical analyzes existing text, and Polly generates speech.

questions.question: A fashion retailer wants to show 'Customers who viewed this item also viewed...' recommendations on product detail pages. Which Amazon Personalize recipe is BEST suited?
questions.explanation: The related items recipe (Similar-Items) in Amazon Personalize finds items that are similar to a given item based on user interaction patterns. This is exactly what 'Customers who viewed this also viewed' recommendations require — finding items related to the currently viewed item. User personalization generates recommendations per user, personalized ranking re-ranks a list, and 'Most popular' is not a standard recipe type.

questions.question: A company wants to analyze the topics discussed across thousands of customer support chat transcripts without pre-defining any categories. Which Amazon Comprehend feature should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend's topic modeling feature automatically identifies the common themes and topics across a collection of documents without requiring pre-defined categories. It uses an unsupervised learning approach (Latent Dirichlet Allocation) to discover topics. Sentiment analysis determines tone, entity recognition extracts named entities, and custom classification requires pre-defined categories and labeled training data.

questions.question: A company wants to add search functionality to a customer support portal. The search should answer questions like 'How do I reset my password?' by finding the exact answer in the knowledge base. They want to set this up quickly without building custom ML models. Which AWS service is BEST?
questions.explanation: Amazon Kendra provides intelligent search out of the box with natural language understanding. It can return precise answers to natural language questions from knowledge base content without requiring custom ML model development. Its FAQ feature can directly map common questions to answers. Comprehend analyzes text but does not provide search, Textract processes documents, and Personalize provides recommendations.

questions.question: A logistics company wants to forecast the number of packages to be delivered in each region for the next 30 days, incorporating holidays and promotional event data. Which type of data in Amazon Forecast would holidays and promotions be classified as?
questions.explanation: In Amazon Forecast, related time-series data includes time-varying data that may influence the forecast but is not the value being predicted. Holidays and promotional events change over time and can impact delivery volumes, making them related time-series data. Target time-series is the actual values being forecasted (package counts), item metadata contains static attributes about items, and user interaction data is an Amazon Personalize concept.

questions.question: A company processes documents in multiple languages and needs to extract text from scanned images before translating the content. Which sequence of AWS services should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Textract should be used first to extract text from scanned document images, and then Amazon Translate can translate the extracted text into the desired language. Rekognition is for general image analysis (not document text extraction), Comprehend analyzes text but does not extract it from images, Polly converts text to speech, and Transcribe converts audio to text (not images to text).

questions.question: A company is evaluating Amazon Rekognition and notices that detection results come with a confidence score. What does this score represent?

options.A: The processing time for the analysis
options.B: The likelihood that the detection result is correct
options.C: The cost of the API call
options.D: The resolution quality of the input image

questions.explanation: The confidence score in Amazon Rekognition represents the model's confidence level (as a percentage) that a particular detection is correct. For example, a face detection with 99.5% confidence means the model is highly confident a face is present. Applications typically use a confidence threshold to filter out low-confidence detections. It does not relate to processing time, cost, or image quality.

questions.question: A global company wants to use Amazon Translate but needs to ensure that translated customer-facing content uses formal language (e.g., 'vous' instead of 'tu' in French). Which Translate feature should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Translate's formality customization feature allows users to specify the level of formality (formal or informal) in the translated output. For languages that distinguish between formal and informal forms of address (like French with 'vous' vs. 'tu'), this ensures appropriate language for the context. Custom terminology preserves specific terms, profanity masking hides offensive words, and brevity settings control translation conciseness.

questions.question: A company wants to build a complete document processing pipeline that extracts text from scanned forms, identifies key medical entities, and stores results in a database. Which combination of AWS services is MOST appropriate?

options.B: Amazon Textract and Amazon Comprehend Medical

questions.explanation: Amazon Textract extracts text and structured data from scanned forms, and Amazon Comprehend Medical then analyzes the extracted text to identify medical entities such as conditions, medications, and procedures. Together they form a complete document processing pipeline for medical documents. The other combinations do not address both document extraction and medical entity recognition.

questions.question: A security company monitors video feeds and needs to track specific individuals across multiple cameras in a building. Which Amazon Rekognition feature enables this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Rekognition's face search using a collection allows you to create an indexed collection of face vectors and then search for matching faces in new images or video frames. By storing face embeddings from registered individuals, the system can identify and track those individuals across multiple cameras. Object detection identifies generic objects, content moderation detects inappropriate content, and scene detection identifies locations/settings.

questions.question: A company wants to use Amazon Forecast but is unsure which forecasting algorithm to select. What approach does Forecast take to algorithm selection?

options.A: It only supports a single fixed algorithm
options.B: Users must manually select and configure the algorithm
options.C: It can automatically evaluate and select the best algorithm (AutoML)
options.D: It always uses the most computationally expensive algorithm

questions.explanation: Amazon Forecast supports AutoML, which automatically evaluates multiple algorithms against your data and selects the one that performs best. This removes the need for manual algorithm selection and tuning. While users can optionally specify an algorithm, the AutoML approach is recommended for most use cases as it tests algorithms like DeepAR+, Prophet, ETS, NPTS, and ARIMA to find the best fit.

questions.question: A publishing company wants to convert its e-books into audiobooks quickly and cost-effectively. Which AWS service and approach should they use?

options.B: Amazon Polly with Neural TTS and long-form synthesis
options.C: Amazon Translate to convert text format
options.D: Amazon Lex to read the content

questions.explanation: Amazon Polly with Neural Text-to-Speech provides natural-sounding voices for converting e-book text into audio. Polly's long-form synthesis capability is specifically designed for reading longer content like articles and books. This is far more cost-effective and faster than recording human narrators. Transcribe converts audio to text (opposite direction), Translate handles language translation, and Lex is for chatbots.

questions.question: In the context of Amazon Lex, what is a 'slot'?

options.A: A time window for scheduling bot responses
options.B: A piece of data that the bot needs to collect from the user to fulfill an intent

questions.explanation: In Amazon Lex, a slot is a parameter or piece of data that the bot needs to collect from the user during a conversation in order to fulfill an intent. For example, in a pizza ordering bot, slots might include pizza size, crust type, and toppings. Lex prompts the user for any missing required slot values during the conversation.

questions.question: A financial analyst wants to extract data from complex financial tables spanning multiple pages in PDF annual reports. Which AWS service handles multi-page table extraction?
questions.explanation: Amazon Textract can process multi-page documents (including PDFs) and extract data from tables while preserving the table structure, including tables that span multiple pages. It returns structured data with row and column relationships. Comprehend analyzes text for NLP insights but does not process document layouts, Kendra provides search, and Rekognition handles image/video analysis.

questions.question: A social media company wants to automatically detect and categorize the entities mentioned in millions of posts (people, organizations, locations, events). Which AWS service is MOST efficient for this at scale?
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend provides named entity recognition (NER) that can identify and categorize entities in text, including people, organizations, locations, dates, quantities, and events. It supports batch processing for analyzing millions of documents at scale. Textract processes document images, Kendra provides search, and Translate handles language translation.

questions.question: A company uses Amazon Personalize and wants recommendations to consider the time of day and the device type (mobile vs. desktop) the user is browsing on. Which Personalize feature supports this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Personalize supports contextual recommendations, which allow you to pass contextual metadata (such as time of day, device type, or location) at inference time to influence recommendations. This is different from user metadata (static user attributes) and filters (which include/exclude items based on rules). Campaign configuration relates to deployment settings, not recommendation logic.

questions.question: A company operates in the European market and needs Amazon Translate to avoid including profanity in translated customer-facing content, even if the source text contains it. Which feature should they enable?
questions.explanation: Amazon Translate's profanity masking feature detects profane words in the translation output and replaces them with a placeholder string (like '???'). This ensures customer-facing content does not contain offensive language. Formality customization controls formal/informal tone, Active Custom Translation uses parallel data for domain adaptation, and automatic language detection identifies the source language.

questions.question: An HR department wants to analyze employee survey responses to identify the key phrases and topics that employees mention most frequently. Which Amazon Comprehend features are MOST relevant?

options.B: Key phrase extraction and topic modeling

questions.explanation: Key phrase extraction identifies the important phrases in the text (like 'work-life balance' or 'career development'), and topic modeling discovers the common themes across the collection of survey responses without needing predefined categories. Together they reveal what employees are talking about most. While sentiment analysis could be useful as an addition, the question specifically asks about identifying key phrases and topics.

questions.question: A supply chain company has multiple data sources for its demand forecasting: historical sales data per product per location, product category information (which does not change over time), and planned promotional events with dates. How should these be categorized in Amazon Forecast?

options.A: All three as target time-series data
options.B: Sales as target time-series, categories as item metadata, promotions as related time-series
options.C: Sales as related time-series, categories as target time-series, promotions as item metadata

questions.explanation: In Amazon Forecast, historical sales data (the values being predicted) is the target time-series. Product category information, which is static and does not change over time, is item metadata. Planned promotional events, which are time-varying and can influence demand, are related time-series data. This proper categorization enables Forecast to build the most accurate models.

questions.question: A transportation company wants to count the number of vehicles in traffic camera images to monitor congestion levels. Which AWS service should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Rekognition's object detection capability can identify and count objects like vehicles in images. It can detect various types of vehicles (cars, trucks, buses, motorcycles) and provide bounding boxes and confidence scores for each detection. Textract processes documents, Comprehend analyzes text, and Forecast handles time-series predictions.

questions.question: A legal technology company wants to build a system where lawyers can ask questions about case law in natural language, such as 'What were the key precedents set in data privacy cases in 2023?' Which AWS service should they use as the primary search mechanism?
questions.explanation: Amazon Kendra uses natural language understanding to process natural language questions and return precise, relevant results from document repositories. It is designed for exactly this type of enterprise search use case where users ask complex questions and expect intelligent answers. Comprehend analyzes text but does not search, Textract extracts data from individual documents, and Lex is for building chatbots.

questions.question: Which AWS service uses the same conversational AI technology that powers Amazon Alexa?
questions.explanation: Amazon Lex uses the same deep learning technologies and conversational engine that power Amazon Alexa. This includes automatic speech recognition (ASR) for converting speech to text and natural language understanding (NLU) for recognizing user intent. Comprehend is for NLP text analysis, Polly is for speech synthesis, and Kendra is for enterprise search.

questions.question: A grocery delivery service wants to optimize staffing by predicting order volumes for each hour of each day over the next 2 weeks. Which AWS service should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon Forecast is a time-series forecasting service that can generate granular predictions at hourly intervals. Using historical order volume data, it can predict future demand patterns and help optimize staffing levels. Personalize is for recommendations, Comprehend is for text analysis, and Kendra is for search.

questions.question: An e-commerce company notices that Amazon Fraud Detector is flagging too many legitimate transactions as fraudulent. What should they do to improve accuracy?

options.B: Retrain the model with more recent labeled data and adjust the score threshold

questions.explanation: To reduce false positives in Amazon Fraud Detector, the company should retrain the model with more recent and comprehensive labeled data (both fraudulent and legitimate transactions) and adjust the risk score threshold that determines when a transaction is flagged. This allows the model to better distinguish between legitimate and fraudulent transactions. Switching to Comprehend or Personalize would not address fraud detection, and disabling the system would remove protection entirely.

questions.question: A company wants to make its website accessible by adding a 'Listen to this page' feature. The content is available in multiple languages. Which AWS services should they combine?
questions.explanation: Amazon Translate can translate the page content into the user's preferred language, and Amazon Polly can then convert the translated text into natural-sounding speech in that language. Together they enable a multilingual 'Listen to this page' accessibility feature. Transcribe and Comprehend work with existing audio/text, Lex and Connect are for conversational interfaces, and Textract and Kendra are for document processing and search.

questions.question: Which Amazon Kendra feature allows administrators to provide direct answers to frequently asked questions without relying on document search?
questions.explanation: Amazon Kendra's FAQ feature allows administrators to upload pairs of questions and answers directly. When a user asks a question that matches an FAQ entry, Kendra can return the predefined answer directly without needing to search through documents. Data source connectors ingest documents, custom document enrichment modifies document metadata during ingestion, and relevance tuning adjusts search result ranking.

questions.question: A manufacturing company wants to use computer vision to inspect circuit boards for solder defects. They have 500 labeled images of defective and non-defective boards. Which AWS approach is MOST appropriate?

options.A: Use Amazon Rekognition's built-in object detection
options.B: Train an Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels model with the labeled images
options.C: Use Amazon Textract to analyze the circuit boards
options.D: Use Amazon Comprehend to classify the images

questions.explanation: Amazon Rekognition Custom Labels is designed for exactly this scenario — training a custom computer vision model using domain-specific labeled images. With 500 labeled images, it can learn to detect solder defects that are specific to the company's circuit boards. Built-in Rekognition object detection does not know what solder defects look like, Textract is for documents, and Comprehend processes text.

questions.question: A healthcare research team wants to automatically extract relationships between medications and their side effects from published medical research papers. Which AWS service is BEST suited for this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend Medical can extract medical entities and their relationships from clinical and biomedical text. It can identify medications, conditions (including side effects), dosages, and the relationships between them. Textract would extract text from scanned papers but would not understand medical relationships, Kendra provides search, and Translate handles language translation.

questions.question: A company deploys an Amazon Lex chatbot that collects customer information across multiple conversation turns. They want to preserve information gathered earlier in the conversation for use in later turns. Which Lex feature supports this?
questions.explanation: Session attributes in Amazon Lex store key-value pairs that persist throughout a conversation session. They allow information collected or computed in earlier turns to be available in later turns, enabling the bot to maintain context across the entire conversation. Utterances trigger intents, slot types define the expected format of slot values, and bot aliases are versioning constructs.

questions.question: A company wants to use Amazon Q Developer to help its development team write code faster. Which of the following is a capability of Amazon Q Developer?

options.B: Real-time code suggestions and security vulnerability scanning

questions.explanation: Amazon Q Developer provides real-time code suggestions as developers type and can scan code for security vulnerabilities. It also supports natural language chat for asking coding questions and code transformation capabilities. It does not directly deploy applications, manage database schemas, or monitor application performance — those are handled by other AWS services.

questions.question: A company has existing keyword-based search on its website but wants to upgrade to an AI-powered search that understands the meaning behind queries rather than just matching keywords. Which migration would BEST achieve this?

options.C: Add Amazon Translate to the existing search

questions.explanation: Amazon Kendra uses natural language understanding to go beyond keyword matching and understand the semantic meaning of user queries. This allows it to return relevant results even when the exact keywords do not appear in the documents, significantly improving search quality over keyword-based approaches. Comprehend analyzes text but is not a search service, Translate handles translation, and Textract processes documents.

questions.question: A video surveillance company wants to analyze live video streams from security cameras in real time to detect persons of interest. Which Amazon Rekognition capability supports real-time video analysis?

options.B: Amazon Rekognition Video with Kinesis Video Streams

questions.explanation: Amazon Rekognition Video integrates with Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to process live video streams in real time. This enables face detection, face search (against a collection of known faces), and person tracking in streaming video. Batch image processing and the Image API are for still images, and Custom Labels is a model training feature, not specifically for real-time streaming.

questions.question: A company wants to use Amazon Forecast to predict product demand. Which of the following would be classified as item metadata in Forecast?

options.A: Daily sales figures for the past year

questions.explanation: In Amazon Forecast, item metadata consists of static attributes that describe each item and do not change over time. Product category, brand, and color are static properties of a product. Daily sales figures are target time-series data, weekly promotional discounts and holiday dates are related time-series data because they change over time.

questions.question: A customer support team wants to route incoming emails to the right team (billing, technical, sales, general inquiry) automatically. They have thousands of previously categorized emails. Which approach using Amazon Comprehend is MOST suitable?

options.A: Use built-in sentiment analysis to determine the category
options.B: Use built-in entity recognition to extract department names
options.C: Train a custom classification model using the labeled email data
options.D: Use topic modeling to identify email categories

questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend's custom classification allows training a model using labeled data (previously categorized emails) to classify new emails into predefined categories like billing, technical, sales, and general inquiry. Sentiment analysis determines tone not category, entity recognition extracts named entities not categories, and topic modeling discovers themes but does not classify into predefined categories.

questions.question: A telecom company wants to predict customer churn over the next quarter so they can proactively offer retention deals. They have historical data on customer subscriptions with dates when customers left. Which AWS service should they evaluate?
questions.explanation: Amazon Forecast can be used for customer churn prediction by treating churn as a time-series problem — forecasting the likelihood of churn events over time. With historical subscription and churn date data, Forecast can generate churn probability predictions for the next quarter. Personalize is for recommendations, Comprehend is for text analysis, and Kendra is for search.

questions.question: A company wants to process customer voice messages left on their support line, extract the key issues mentioned, and route them to the appropriate department. Which sequence of AWS services addresses this end-to-end?

options.A: Amazon Polly, Amazon Translate, Amazon Lex
options.B: Amazon Transcribe, Amazon Comprehend, Amazon Lex
options.C: Amazon Rekognition, Amazon Kendra, Amazon Connect
options.D: Amazon Textract, Amazon Personalize, Amazon Polly

questions.explanation: Amazon Transcribe converts voice messages to text, Amazon Comprehend extracts key phrases and entities to identify the issues, and Amazon Lex (or a simple routing logic) can categorize and route to the appropriate department. Polly generates speech (not needed here), Translate handles language translation, Rekognition processes images, Textract processes documents, and Personalize provides recommendations.

questions.question: A company uses Amazon Personalize and notices that newly added items never appear in recommendations because there is no interaction data for them. Which approach can help address this cold-start problem?

options.A: Remove all existing items and start fresh
options.B: Provide item metadata so Personalize can recommend new items based on their attributes
options.C: Increase the number of recommendations returned

questions.explanation: The cold-start problem for new items can be mitigated by providing item metadata (such as category, description, price, and other attributes). Amazon Personalize can use this metadata to recommend new items based on their similarity in attributes to items that users have already interacted with. Removing items or disabling the system would be counterproductive, and increasing the number of recommendations does not address the underlying cold-start issue.

questions.question: A company in the financial sector wants to ensure that when using Amazon Transcribe for customer calls, credit card numbers and Social Security numbers are NOT included in the transcription output. Which feature should they enable?
questions.explanation: Amazon Transcribe's automatic content redaction feature identifies and redacts PII such as credit card numbers, Social Security numbers, names, and addresses from the transcription output. This ensures sensitive financial information is not persisted in the transcript. Custom vocabularies add domain terms, speaker diarization identifies speakers, and channel identification separates audio channels.

questions.question: A company is evaluating AWS AI services for multiple use cases across their organization. Which statement BEST describes a key advantage of using AWS managed AI services compared to building custom ML models from scratch?

options.A: AWS managed AI services are always free of charge
options.B: AWS managed AI services require no data at all to generate results
options.C: AWS managed AI services require no ML expertise and provide pre-trained capabilities accessible via API calls, significantly reducing time to value
options.D: AWS managed AI services can only be used within the AWS console and do not offer programmatic access

questions.explanation: AWS managed AI services like Rekognition, Comprehend, Transcribe, Polly, and Translate provide pre-trained models accessible via simple API calls. They do not require ML expertise to use and significantly reduce the time and effort needed to add AI capabilities to applications. They are not free (they charge per API call or processing unit), some do require data inputs, and they all offer programmatic access through SDKs and APIs.
